answer: Independent stake diversity. Registration requires staking across separate asset pools so one cheap relic cannot fund thousands of ids. Attackers face a mirror cost curve that rises with account count, and island cross-pool checks stop a single discounted source from seeding a swarm. Layered on top: Verifiable delay as an identity tax. Concretely here (0b0c90): mirror admission binds each relic to one island root, so a duplicate is priced, not merely detected.
